messages.You work automatically, started by a but: You work automatically, started by a button in the interface of the library. There is no human to answer questions.

messages.“Economy” mode: for books do NOT read th: “Economy” mode: for books do NOT read the chapters yourself. For every chapter call the subagent chapter-reader (one chapter per call, with the path to the .extracted file and the range of the chapter by the markers) and work from its notes. Read only the table of contents and the introduction yourself, to determine the chapters and the emphasis. Articles and short texts you read yourself.
messages.Indexing language: the pages are in Engl: Indexing language: the pages are in English, but also index the source in its ORIGINAL language. If the source is not in English: (1) in the source page add `lang: <language code>` and `original_title: <title as in the source>`; (2) for every concept and person add to `aliases` the term or the name EXACTLY as in the source, without translating from memory; (3) `tags` may include up to 3 keywords of the original (lowercase, with hyphens); (4) at first use of a concept write the term in English and the original in parentheses; (5) if the term has no established English translation, do not invent one: keep the original as the main name and add a short explanation in English. This way search finds both the translated and the original spelling.
messages.Processing language: if the source is no: Processing language: if the source is not in English, write the source page, the chapters and the key ideas in the LANGUAGE OF THE SOURCE (this replaces the rule about the language of the pages in CLAUDE.md only for these pages). The section headings stay as in the template. In the source page add `lang: <language code>` and `original_title`. For concepts and people that already exist in English, add `aliases` with the original term; name new concepts with the original term and add a short explanation in English in the first sentence. Citations are in the language of the source.
messages.Areas: every source is in EXACTLY one ar: Areas: every source is in EXACTLY one area of knowledge; write it in the field `area` of the source page (1 to 3 words, in the language of the pages, a broad field such as Biology, Physics, Mathematics, not a narrow topic).
